entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1 . RAJAT YADAV S/O VINOD YADAV, AGED ABOUT  25 YEARS, OCCUPATION: SERVICE, R/O: 118/6  FIROZ GANDHI NAGAR, INDORE (MADHYA  PRADESH)

2 . STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH P.S.
 VIJAY NAGAR THROUGH P.S. VIJAY NAGAR,
 INDORE (MADHYA PRADESH)

.
 (MR. MADHUSUDAN YADAV - ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.1 AND  MS. VARSHA SINGH THAKUR - PUBLIC PROSECUTOR FOR THE  RESPONDENT NO.2/STATE)

This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER Counsel for both the parties heard.

2. Applicant / prosecutrix has filed this application under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. for cancellation of bail granted to the respondent No.1 / accused vide order dated 22.09.2023 passed in MCRC No.41230/2023 by this Court, on the ground that respondent No.1 is harassing and threatening the prosecutrix and other witnesses.

3 . Learned counsel for the applicant contended that offence under Sections 366, 354-A, 354-D, 323,
294, 506 and 376 of IPC has been registered against the respondent No.1 and by the aforesaid order Prosecutrix vs Rajat Yadav on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180284036/
1 this Court has granted bail to him, but he has failed to comply the conditions of the bail bond.

He is continuously threatening and pressurizing the prosecutrix to enter into a compromise and due to the harassment given by respondent No.1, prosecutrix has lodged the FIR against respondent No.1 and has also made the written complaint against him.
Hence, he prays that application be allowed and the bail granted to the respondent No.1 be cancelled and the respondent No.2/State be directed to take the respondent No.1 into custody forthwith.
4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 opposes the prayer.

5 . Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 / State submits that prosecutrix was threatened and pressurized by respondent No.1 and after releasing on bail respondent No.1 has committed another offence.
Accordingly, offence under Sections 294 and 506 of IPC has been registered against him and by doing so he has violated the terms and conditions of the bail bond.

6 . Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties and from perusal of the earlier bail order passed in favour of the respondent No.1, it reveals that prosecutrix / applicant lodged an FIR against the respondent No.1, and on her report offence under Sections 294 and 506 of IPC has been registered against the respondent No.1 on 06.11.2023 vide crime No.604/2023, thereafter, she has also made a written complaint against the respondent No.1.
Applicant has filed so many documents that respondent No.1 was harassing her by sending obscene messages, due to which her marriage has been broken.

In view of the aforesaid, it reveals that after releasing on bail, respondent No.1 was continuously threatening her to enter into a compromise and was sending obscene massages, due to which marriage of the prosecutrix has been broken.
Accordingly, an offence under Sections 294 and 506 of IPC has also been registered against the respondent No.1.

7. In view of the above, it is clear that respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of his bail bond and strong ground is made out for cancellation of bail.
8 .

Accordingly, this application under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. for cancellation of bail is allowed and bail given to the respondent No.1 vide order dated 22.09.2023 passed in MCRC No.41230/2023 is hereby cancelled and respondent No.2 / State is directed to arrest the respondent No.1 immediately and he be taken into custody.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Prosecutrix vs Rajat Yadav on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180284036/
